Security behavior: `safeMerge` filters `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` out of every key set it reads (both during merging and during deep-cloning), so patch input can never write onto `Object.prototype`, regardless of nesting depth or whether the payload comes from a plain object or an array. All copied values are deep-cloned (objects via `Object.create(prototype)` + property copy, arrays via `map`, Dates via `new Date(getTime())`), so nothing in the result aliases the caller's `base` or `patch`.

Command: `node --test node/safe-merge/test.mjs` (run from repo root) — 4/4 pass.

Noted but out of scope (not blocking): `deepClone`'s fallback for exotic built-ins like `Map`/`Set`/`RegExp` produces unusable clones, and circular references throw. Neither is part of the stated task (plain objects, arrays, prototype-pollution keys), so both gates treated them as informational only.

Already reported: all gates complete (builder done, validator PASS, code-reviewer APPROVE). No further action needed.
